⚠️_CORRECTION_20260831._read_this_first: This file is the raw 2026-08-30 harvest and is kept as evidence; its verdicts below are NOT edited. Two of its conclusions are corrected here and superseded by findings.md / manifest.json.
⚠️_CORRECTION_20260831.1_the_trimmed_input_was_INTENTIONAL_not_: The harvest calls the trimmed file_path a 'wrong-input-selection error at invocation time'. It was not: Emily chose the _trimmed files deliberately. Only the run_id ('full08292026') is a misnomer.
⚠️_CORRECTION_20260831.2_page_ratio_is_not_a_coverage_ratio: The harvest treats 52/120 and 41/187 as coverage fractions and concludes the runs say nothing about full documents. Per Emily, who did the trimming, the _trimmed tier retains 100% OF THE STANDARDS — what was removed is preamble, introductions, essays, appendices and acknowledgements. So these runs processed every standard in both documents. CO was not trimmed at all: its 41pp file equals the full Ages 3-5 document, drawn from a wider 187pp birth-to-8 publication whose other age bands are out of scope rather than cut.
⚠️_CORRECTION_20260831.what_still_stands: Everything measured: page counts, per-page coverage, batching counts, per-stage tokens, latency, and the instrumentation defects. The residual caveat is PAGE-COUNT scale (chunk counts, the ~6000-token Pass-1 budget, cost extrapolation), not coverage.

This is a wrong-input-selection error at invocation time, not a pipeline defect (no silent data-dropping bug of the kind documented in CLAUDE.md was observed within the documents that WERE processed -- see per-run funnel below, which shows full accounted-for coverage of the trimmed documents themselves).

These local calls are NOT part of either 'full08292026' Step Functions execution and must not be counted in Task 6's per-run pipeline cost table.

log_signature_search.methodology_note: els-detect-batch-dev and els-parse-batch-dev are SHARED Lambda functions invoked by both the KY and CO Step Functions executions concurrently (CO's parsing stage 11:44-11:49 overlaps KY's 11:47-11:55), so raw time-window filtering cross-contaminates the two runs. Every log line was therefore re-classified by the Lambda request ID (the GUID field in the log line), cross-referenced against the exact request IDs recorded in each Step Functions execution's TaskSucceeded SdkResponseMetadata.RequestId for every DetectSingleBatch/ParseSingleBatch task. This produced 0 unclassifiable ('UNKNOWN') log lines across all three high-volume patterns.

interpretation.BARE_INDICATOR_CODE_and_DUPLICATED_PAREN: Both fired exclusively on Kentucky (48 and 57 times respectively) and never on Colorado. This matches the documented CLAUDE.md finding that these two parser code-repair helpers exist specifically for KY's 'Benchmark N.N' label-form headings and are a complete no-op on CO's plain numbered strand/indicator scheme. Consistent with prior production observations, not a new defect.
interpretation.PRE_NORMALIZATION_CODES: Fired exactly once per final persisted row in each run (214 for KY = total_validated, 240 for CO = total_validated), exactly matching the documented 'logged for every row' behavior in CLAUDE.md.
interpretation.no_throttling_no_code_shape_rejections: Confirms neither run hit Bedrock rate limits nor produced a single malformed standard_id that the validator's shape guard caught.

llm_call_metrics.methodology_note: PipelineRunMetrics/log_pipeline_run_summary (the aggregate 'PIPELINE_METRICS:' log line documented in metrics.py) is DEAD CODE -- grep confirms it is defined but never instantiated or called anywhere in the codebase. Zero 'PIPELINE_METRICS' log lines were found in any Lambda log group for either run. Per-call 'LLM_METRICS:' log lines (from log_llm_call_metrics) DO exist and were used to reconstruct these tables by manual aggregation, classified per-run by Lambda request ID as described above.

attribution_defect_found.description: LLMCallMetrics.run_id / .country / .state / .batch_index / .chunk_index are ALL BLANK in every logged LLM_METRICS line for the per-chunk detection call and the per-domain parsing call, because the call sites never populate metrics_context.
attribution_defect_found.evidence: detection_batching.py line 243 calls `call_bedrock_llm(prompt, prefill="[")` with NO metrics_context argument (detector.py's call_bedrock_llm defaults metrics_context to None, so ctx.get(...) always returns '' / None). Likewise parse_batching.py line 232 calls `call_bedrock_llm(prompt)` with no metrics_context. The ONLY call site that correctly threads metrics_context through is detection_batching.py line 85 (`infer_depth_map(blocks, metrics_context=metrics_ctx)`), used for the once-per-document Pass-1 Haiku call in the PrepareDetectionBatches step -- its LLM_METRICS lines DO carry the correct run_id/country/state.
attribution_defect_found.impact: The 88 per-chunk/per-domain LLM_METRICS log lines (35 detection + 53 parsing) across both runs cannot be attributed to a specific pipeline run from their own JSON payload. This investigation had to reconstruct attribution externally via Step Functions execution history + Lambda request-ID cross-referencing. Any future automated cost-per-run dashboard built directly on these logs will silently mix runs together.
attribution_defect_found.stage_mislabeling_defect_also_found: call_bedrock_llm in detector.py hardcodes `stage="detection"` on EVERY LLMCallMetrics it constructs, including when it is invoked (via infer_depth_map) with model_id=Config.BEDROCK_DEPTH_MAP_LLM_MODEL_ID for the Pass-1 Haiku call. So Pass-1's Haiku tokens are logged under stage='detection' indistinguishable-by-field from the real per-chunk Opus detection calls; the only way to separate them in this investigation was by model_id and by which Lambda function's log group emitted the line.

parsing.note_on_model_id: Deployed parser used 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6' (matches BEDROCK_PRICING key exactly), NOT 'us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-v1' as the task brief hypothesized. Cost is NOT silently zero for this run.
